subject: POC economics: budget bands & latency tradeoffs (post-call)

Subject: POC economics: budget bands & latency tradeoffs (post-call)

Hi Anna — great to meet you and team on the call earlier. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can align on a pilot that fits OpsCo's constraints.

Recap of what we heard (please correct anything):
- Monthly volume: you mentioned a range ~10–30M tokens (spiky days) with an initial pilot expected at ~5–8M tokens.
- Latency target: p95 300–500ms for the interactive search UI; batch scoring can tolerate 1–3s.
- Budget range for 1st month pilot: $8k–$15k (Ops/Procurement preference to stay under $15k).
- Compliance: standard SOC2 acceptable, data retention must be configurable.

Primary ask from Redwood: confirm the priority between (1) strict latency SLOs for end-users vs (2) unit-cost target ($ / 1M tokens). Example: is your target closer to $50/1M tokens or are you willing to pay up to $120/1M for sub-400ms p95?

Two candidate pilot configurations (high-level):

- Latency-first (Tier L):
  - Streaming endpoint, dedicated capacity (small reserved pool), minimal batching, KV prefix cache enabled.
  - Expected p95: ~200–350ms for short prompts.
  - Estimated unit economics: ~$95–$130 per 1M tokens (depends on model variant).
  - Good when user experience is primary and budget is flexible.

- Cost-first (Tier C):
  - Mixed-mode: async batch for heavy scoring, continuous batching for interactive with slightly higher tail latency, quantized model variant (int8).
  - Expected p95: ~400–800ms (more variance); much lower cost per token.
  - Estimated unit economics: ~$38–$55 per 1M tokens (model and quantization dependent).

Attachments: attached a short band playbook and a pilot estimate workbook for the ranges above.

Next steps I propose:
1) Anna / OpsCo: confirm which pilot priority best matches Procurement (latency-first vs cost-first) and the pilot target volume (we can size accordingly).
2) Redwood: once you confirm, Grace will send an opex estimate and the configuration we'll spin up for a 2-week pilot.
3) OpsCo: confirm compliance checklist items we must include for pilot.

If helpful, we can run a hybrid pilot: route 20% of traffic to Tier L for live UX tests and 80% to Tier C to validate unit economics. That gives you both signal without full price exposure.

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Dylan — good write-up, and apologies for the follow-up emails from our side as we sort internal numbers. A few clarifications from OpsCo: 

- Volume: pilot target will be 6–10M tokens (we want a two-week stress window + live-test window). Longer term (Q4) we expect 20–25M tokens monthly if the pilot succeeds.
- Budget: Procurement prefers to see pilot under $15k total. For expansion we have flexibility but need clear unit-cost targets to forecast.
- Latency: product team prefers p95 <= 400ms for interactive search; batch scoring is lower priority. If we had to choose, we'd prioritize the p95 SLA for the interactive path.
- Compliance: please include a short note on data retention options and KMS integration for the pilot. SOC2 report is required for any paid pilot.

Can you send a one-page recommendation for the pilot config (one latency-first option and one cost-first option) plus a sample estimate table that maps token volumes to monthly cost? Also share how we'd measure ‘success’ for the pilot.

Thanks — assigning Rekha (cc) to coordinate procurement checks.

Best,
Anna

Subject: Re: POC economics: budget bands & latency tradeoffs (post-call)

Hi Anna — quick technical proposal and concrete numbers so Procurement has something to review. I split it into the two pilot routes Dylan suggested, plus a hybrid option.

Summary of trade-offs (short):
- Streaming (low-latency): favors reserved GPUs, small batch sizes, and aggressive KV caching. Best UX; higher $/token because of reserved capacity and lower batching efficiency.
- Continuous batching / async scoring: amortizes GPU work across many requests; best $/token but increased tail latency and variance.
- Quantization (int8 / mixed): typically reduces runtime cost 30–60% on compatible models with minor quality delta for many tasks.

Concrete pilot configurations and back-of-envelope economics (estimates for pilot months; actual will vary by model choice):

1) Latency-first pilot (Recommendation if p95 <= 400ms is mandatory)\- Model: redwood-v1-stream (optimized kernels)\- Infra: Dedicated small pool (2 reserved workers, burst autoscale to 4)\- Endpoint: streaming, prefix/KV cache enabled\- Expected p95: 200–350ms interactive\- Pilot volume: 8M tokens\- Estimated cost: ~ $920 for infra baseline + $7,200 token charges => ~ $8,120 total (~$1,015 / 1M tokens)

Note: the above includes reserved pool amortized across the month; for a two-week pilot we'll pro-rate. If we remove dedicated reservation and run on shared capacity, latency tail risks increase but token-only costs drop substantially.

2) Cost-first pilot (Recommendation if strict budget ceiling required)\- Model: redwood-v1-batch (quantized int8)\- Infra: mixed-mode (continuous batching + spot capacity)\- Endpoint: async scoring for bulk; small continuous batch for interactive path\- Expected p95: 450–800ms interactive\- Pilot volume: 8M tokens\- Estimated cost: infra baseline ~$320 + token charges ~$360 => ~$680 total (~$85 / 1M tokens)

3) Hybrid pilot (practical compromise)\- Route 20% of interactive traffic to Latency-first endpoint and 80% to Cost-first path.\- Expected blended p95: ~350–420ms; blended unit cost: mid-point ~$250 / 1M tokens for pilot (higher than pure cost-first due to reservation overhead).

How we measure success (suggested KPIs for pilot):
- UX KPI: interactive p95 <= 400ms for at least 95% of requests to the latency-first route.
- Econ KPI: steady-state blended unit cost < $350 / 1M tokens for pilot (or meet Procurement’s budget cap).
- Quality KPI: model output coherence measured on a 50-case eval suite with <5% regression vs baseline rules.

Docs and artifacts attached: OpsCo_POC_Band_Playbook.pdf (one-page playbook) and a pilot-estimate.xlsx with token-to-cost mappings and a pro-rate calculator. I also dropped an example HubSpot opportunity with estimated line items in the shared Drive link.

If OpsCo wants the cheapest per-1M token number, we’ll pick a larger batch window and run an aggressively quantized variant. If you need the live UX, we should accept the higher per-token price for the latency-first route.

Happy to walk through the numbers on a short call — suggest Tuesday 7/20 at 10am PT.

—
